evidence.quote: I had a long letter from a ship-mate in Australia, who says the Colony is getting decidedly republican, from the influx of Americans, & that all the great & novel schemes for working the Gold are planned & executed by these men.
evidence.assessment: Darwin reports the content second-hand as a long letter from an Australian ship-mate; P5 does not name the ship-mate, date the incoming letter, or identify a surviving enclosure/transcription.

preserved_candidates.title: To Syms Covington 23 November 1850
preserved_candidates.assessment: Not the incoming source: it is Darwin’s outgoing acknowledgment of a Covington box and specimens. The body discusses specimen richness and old papers used as packing, with no republicanism/American immigration/gold-working report.

preserved_candidates.title: To Syms Covington 14 March 1852
preserved_candidates.assessment: Not the incoming source: Darwin asks about Covington’s move toward the gold mines and the Geelong beds, but the surviving body is Darwin’s outgoing question and does not supply the reported republicanism/American schemes.

preserved_candidates.title: To Syms Covington 21 October 1853
preserved_candidates.assessment: Not the incoming source: Darwin acknowledges Covington’s 25 May 1853 letter and asks about the Ovens diggings and mining effects, but this source contains no incoming Covington prose and no identified republicanism/American gold-scheme passage.

preserved_candidates.title: To Syms Covington 28 February 1855
preserved_candidates.assessment: Not the incoming source: Darwin acknowledges Covington’s 8 August 1854 letter and reports news from the gold districts via Mackenzie. It is a later outgoing witness, not the ship-mate letter described in 1553, and does not mention republicanism or American-led schemes.

finding: No preserved Covington-to-Darwin source matching the specific P5 report was located in all_letters.jsonl. The available Covington records are Darwin outgoings; they establish that Covington wrote to Darwin on other occasions but cannot identify the unnamed ship-mate letter or prove its receipt date/content beyond Darwin’s report.
relationship_status: knowledge_witness_only; no direct reply pair and no incoming endpoint identified
retrieval_limit: The preserved collection has no source-complete incoming Syms Covington letter in the searched records. Further retrieval would require an external/archive source request; no network fetch was made.
notes: All candidate outgoing bodies were read fully with their date metadata and apparatus projection.
Shared Australian gold topic and the presence of other Covington letters are insufficient to substitute an outgoing source for the missing incoming letter.
